scope: Deduplicated publisher-verified peer-reviewed primary measured injection-moulding evidence. Reviews, simulation-only work, synthetic-only data and duplicate publications/companion datasets from the same experiment do not inflate the primary measured count.

credibilityPolicy.tierA: Peer-reviewed primary measured study with a public raw or companion measured dataset whose provenance is tied to the experiment.
credibilityPolicy.tierB: Publisher-verified peer-reviewed primary measured study with real experimental/production measurements and physical quality outcomes, but reusable raw data are not confirmed public or are request-only.

promotionCandidates.independenceRationale: The two qualifying papers are distinct experimental programmes with different author teams and different fibre-processing architectures: conventional highly reinforced long-fibre polypropylene injection moulding versus direct-fibre-feeding GF/PP with redesigned mixing elements. They do not re-analyse or duplicate one moulding campaign, and both independently measure retained fibre morphology/length together with physical mechanical outcomes.
promotionCandidates.boundedClaim: Measured injection-moulding history and plasticising/mixing architecture can change retained fibre length and therefore mechanical response. Do not promote any tested screw, mixing-element, fibre-length or process value as a universal limit or setting.

promotionCandidates.independenceRationale: These are separate multicavity experimental programmes from distinct research teams: one varies runner/gate geometry and polymer viscosity while measuring cavity-specific fill and mechanical outcomes, while the other uses multiple in-mould sensors and controlled switchover/holding/clamping experiments to observe local cavity behaviour. They are not duplicate publications or re-analyses of a shared dataset.
promotionCandidates.boundedClaim: Geometric balance does not guarantee rheological balance; cavity-resolved pressure/fill and physical outcomes are needed before averaging multicavity behaviour. Do not promote runner size, gate size, pressure or balance values as universal design limits.

promotionCandidates.independenceRationale: The counted LSR studies are distinct experiments from different teams and years: the 2023 programme characterises cross-linking/cure state through cavity-pressure and DSC evidence, while the 2014 programme varies processing conditions and measures cavity pressure/temperature together with tensile strength. They are separate experimental programmes rather than duplicate publications or re-analysis of the same moulding campaign.
promotionCandidates.boundedClaim: LSR cure/cross-linking produces measurable cavity-pressure/thermal signatures tied to physical material or mechanical outcomes. Do not promote any cure time, cavity pressure, mould temperature or strength value as a universal LSR prescription.

promotionCandidates.independenceRationale: The two qualifying studies are separate material-conditioning and injection-moulding experiments from different research teams. One uses measured residual moisture with controlled plasticisation experiments on TPU/PC and physical appearance outcomes; the other independently examines PA/TPU drying/residual-moisture condition and moulded quality defects. They are not duplicate publications or re-analysis of one dataset.
promotionCandidates.boundedClaim: Measured material moisture/drying state can alter moulded-part quality and must be distinguished from a dryer setpoint alone. Do not promote any moisture percentage, dryer temperature or residence time as a universal material limit; supplier grade data remain authoritative for production.

promotionCandidates.independenceRationale: The qualifying studies are distinct experimental programmes from separate teams and tooling contexts: one applies a factorial process study and multi-scale metrology to randomly micro-textured mouldings, while the other uses variothermal PMMA microfluidic replication with independently measured cavity-surface temperature and in-cavity melt pressure. They do not duplicate or re-analyse the same moulding experiment.
promotionCandidates.boundedClaim: Surface replication depends on local thermal/pressure history, feature scale, polymer and tool surface; measured physical replication should be used instead of appearance assumptions. Do not promote tested temperatures, pressures, feature ratios or timing as universal replication settings.

promotionCandidates.independenceRationale: These are independent precision-optics injection-compression programmes with different authors, polymers and geometries: a 2023 plastic lens-array experiment measures optical path difference, displacement, birefringence and imaging quality, while a 2013 PS/PC disk programme experimentally measures residual birefringence alongside simulation. They are separate experiments, not duplicate publications or re-analysis of the same data.
promotionCandidates.boundedClaim: Injection-compression history can materially affect residual birefringence, dimensional and optical performance, so precision optics requires physical optical/stress metrology. Do not promote compression gap, timing, temperature, pressure or birefringence values as universal production limits.
